chat: Did your grandfather have an operation?

Yes, he is operated on last month.
Yes, he was operated on last month.

questions.source: There was a lack of technology. Major surgery could not develop.
options: There was a lack of technology, so major surgery can not develop.
So there was a lack of technology, major surgery could not develop.
There was a lack of technology, so major surgery could not develop.
questions.rule: so comes before the result clause, and the tense stays the same: could not develop.

questions.source: Neurosurgery is the most difficult branch of surgery.
options: Neurosurgery is more difficult than any branch of surgery.
Neurosurgery is more difficult than any other branch of surgery.
Neurosurgery is most difficult than any other branch of surgery.

options: Neither the doctor nor the nurses were tired.

Neither the doctor nor the nurses was tired.
questions.rule: neither ... nor; the verb agrees with the nearer subject (nurses → were).

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.

chat: Why did you miss the school bus?

The bus had already go when I got to the corner.
The bus had already gone when I got to the corner.

chat: Who will help with the science exhibition, you or Kunal?
options: Both Kunal and I will help.

Both Kunal or I will help.
questions.rule: both ... and; as a subject, use I, not 'me'.

questions.source: Cardiac surgery was tried in the past. Patients did not survive.

Cardiac surgery was tried in the past, but did patients not survive.
Cardiac surgery was tried in the past, but patients did not survive.
questions.rule: but joins two contrasting clauses; each keeps its normal order and tense.

questions.source: Robotic surgery is precise. It is also less painful.
options: Robotic surgery is not only precise and also less painful.
Not only robotic surgery is precise but also less painful.
Robotic surgery is not only precise but also less painful.
questions.rule: Put not only and but also before the two matching words: precise / less painful.
